FLINK-38093.title: [FLINK-38093][k8s] Bump Fabric8 version to 7.3.1
FLINK-38093.description:
## What is the purpose of the change

Upgrade Fabric8 Kubernetes client to 7.3.1, which is the latest version as of creating this PR. 

The new version has changed the default HTTP client implementation from OkHttp to Vert.x, which I have reverted as well to stay consistent with previous versions. We can look into using Vert.x in another task.

## Brief change log

- Upgrade Fabric8 version
- Shade artifacts that should not be included in the JAR
- Add override of netty-codec-http as the test package kubernetes-server-mock use Vert.x, which depends on a newer version of Netty that we currently have. This can be removed once Netty is upgraded to at least 4.1.108.Final

## Verifying this change

Built image locally and tested it with Flink Kubernetes Operator

## What is the purpose of the change

This pull request adds HTTP protocol support to OpenTelemetry reporters (metrics, events, and traces) in addition to the existing gRPC support.


## Brief change log

- Added HTTP protocol support to OpenTelemetryMetricReporter, OpenTelemetryEventReporter, and OpenTelemetryTraceReporter
- Introduced new configuration option `exporter.protocol` with values `gRPC (default)` and `HTTP`
- Added tests for gRPC and HTTP protocols Otel Reporters
- Made OtelTestContainer class public for testing


## Verifying this change

This change added tests and can be verified as follows:

- Added `OpenTelemetryMetricReporterProtocolTest` to verify `HTTP` and `gRPC` protocol support for metrics
- Added `OpenTelemetryEventReporterProtocolTest` to verify events
- Added `OpenTelemetryTraceReporterProtocolTest` to verify traces
- Created `AbstractOpenTelemetryReporterProtocolTest` base class with test scenarios including case-insensitive protocol specification
- All tests verify that data is properly exported using both protocols

FLINK-38352.title: [FLINK-38352][table-planner] Make source specs forward compatible (like sink specs) | [FLINK-38352][table] Expose timestamp used in DefaultWatermarkGenerator
FLINK-38352.description:
=== PR #27006 (1/2) ===
## What is the purpose of the change

For consistency reason, `WatermarkPushDownSpec` can be forward-compatible. While implementing this, I noticed that all sinks specs are forward compatible but not the source specs. This adds consistency. A general ignoring of unknown properties should be avoided, however, because this could lead to unintended side effects.

## Brief change log

Add `@JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown = true)` to all source specs


## Verifying this change

This change is a trivial rework / code cleanup without any test coverage.

## Does this pull request potentially affect one of the following parts:

  - Dependencies (does it add or upgrade a dependency): no
  - The public API, i.e., is any changed class annotated with `@Public(Evolving)`: no
  - The serializers: no
  - The runtime per-record code paths (performance sensitive): no
  - Anything that affects deployment or recovery: JobManager (and its components), Checkpointing, Kubernetes/Yarn, ZooKeeper: no
  - The S3 file system connector: no

## Documentation

  - Does this pull request introduce a new feature? no
  - If yes, how is the feature documented? not applicable


---

=== PR #26991 (2/2) ===
## What is the purpose of the change

Access to a time attribute might be code generated as well, esp. when referencing a computed column. This PR allows to access the timestamp generated from the DefaultWatermarkGenerator which might be useful for wrapping watermark strategies that would like to use this internal API.

## Brief change log

Offer an internal API via `DefaultWatermarkGenerator.extractTimestamp`.

## Verifying this change

This change added tests and can be verified as follows:
- `WatermarkGeneratorCodeGenTest`
- Restore tests

## Does this pull request potentially affect one of the following parts:

  - Dependencies (does it add or upgrade a dependency): no

  - The runtime per-record code paths (performance sensitive): no
  - Anything that affects deployment or recovery: JobManager (and its components), Checkpointing, Kubernetes/Yarn, ZooKeeper: no
  - The S3 file system connector: no

## Documentation

  - If yes, how is the feature documented? JavaDocs
